transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because nobody seems to take it seriously that people at work are secretly targeting my projects, even when I show them the evidence. It's incredibly frustrating because I have the proof, but everyone else just brushes it off like I'm making it up.
Besides these concerns about your colleagues, have you been experiencing other symptoms like a persistent loss of interest in activities, low energy, or hearing voices that others cannot hear?

No, I definitely don't hear voices or feel low on energy. I only stopped playing basketball and going to team events because I have to stay on guard to protect my work, not because I've lost interest in things. Outside of that, I still handle my regular tickets, help junior devs, and meet my cousin for pho on weekends like I always have.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to perform your job duties or manage your daily responsibilities since these concerns about your colleagues began?

My actual work performance is fine—I still handle my tickets, help junior devs, and manage my daily life and bills without any issues. However, because I have to stay on guard, I've stopped going to team events, and HR has warned me that my accusations in meetings are putting my position at risk. So while I can do the technical work, my relationships and standing at the company are definitely suffering.
Have you always felt that people are generally untrustworthy or out to get you, even in situations outside of your current workplace?

No, absolutely not. This isn't a lifelong thing, and I don't feel this way about people in general—it only started about nine months ago and is strictly focused on that competing tech team at work. Outside of trying to protect my projects from them, I get along fine with others, like helping junior devs or hanging out with my cousin.
Have you ever had any other experiences where you felt strongly that someone was trying to harm or sabotage you, or is this specific situation at work the only time you've ever felt this way?

No, this is the absolute first and only time I have ever felt this way, and it is strictly limited to this situation at work. It only started about nine months ago during our major cloud migration project when they began sabotaging my code. I am not a paranoid person; this is a very real, isolated threat that I am forced to deal with.

Have you noticed any changes in your speech, such as others telling you that your thoughts are hard to follow or that your sentences don't make sense, or have you noticed any odd behaviors that others have commented on?

No, my speech and communication are completely normal, and no one has ever told me that my thoughts are hard to follow or that my sentences don't make sense. I've always been clear and logical when explaining things, both at work and in my personal life.

latest_inference.note: The patient exhibits a circumscribed, non-bizarre-appearing delusional belief (work sabotage) that has persisted for nine months. The absence of hallucinations, disorganized speech, negative symptoms, or significant functional impairment outside of the specific delusional context makes F20.0 (Schizophrenia) highly unlikely. F22 remains the primary candidate as the symptoms are limited to a specific, non-bizarre theme without broader psychotic features.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent, non-bizarre (though potentially delusional) belief that colleagues are sabotaging their work. The symptoms have lasted for nine months, and there is no evidence of schizophrenia (no hallucinations, no disorganized speech/behavior), mood disorders, or a decline in general functioning outside of the specific delusional focus.
